newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela bolivar ends flat at 482.75/483.75/dlr.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela bolivar ends flat at 482.75/483.75/dlr.

text.p: The Venezuelan bolivar closed flat in balanced trade at 482.75/483.75 per dollar as investors unwound long dollar positions to take advantage of overnight bolivar bank lending rates of between 60 and 75 percent, traders said.
"There were a lot of dollars offered ... as banks burnt their dollar positions to take advantage of the interbank lending rate," said one trader.
On Monday the overnight rate hit 90 percent as investors moved into dollars on fears of an accelerated depreciation of the bolivar.

But Central Bank president Antonio Casas Gonzalez calmed the market Tuesday, traders said, when he said the bolivar would stay stable within the current bands system and that it was not following a hidden "crawling peg" system.
"The Central Bank can't have supplied more than 20 percent of the session's dollar liquidity," said another trader noting that the market had supplied most of its own dollar needs.

Venezuela's foreign exchange market is unusual in that the Central Bank is its largest single supplier of dollars, which blurs the difference between the Central Bank supplying liquidity and intervening.

The market's flow back into bolivars helped bring down the interbank rate to between 60 and 75 percent, traders said, although yields at Wednesday's small, 30 billion bolivar TEM auction are expected to firm on the continuing -- albeit temporary -- liquidity squeeze.
